Documentation-only change. Read the current docs/features/query-plan-analysis.md,
locate the Performance Impact section and the PostgreSQL platform section, and
apply the two corrections above. No code changes.
description:
docs/features/query-plan-analysis.md contains two inaccuracies added by PR #776:

1. Performance overhead table (the "Other platforms: ~10-50ms" claim):
   The table lists "Other platforms (Redshift, PostgreSQL, etc.): ~10-50ms overhead
   per query capture". This is false for PostgreSQL with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
   PostgreSQLAdapter.get_query_plan() uses EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON),
   which physically re-executes the query. The overhead for PostgreSQL is
   approximately 1× query execution time, not a flat 10-50ms. A slow TPC-H query
   (e.g., Q18 at SF=1 can take seconds) would cost double that time with plan
   capture active. The 10-50ms estimate is only valid for platforms that use
   a static EXPLAIN without ANALYZE.

2. DML note in the PostgreSQL section:
   The note says "DML statements (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/COPY) use FORMAT JSON
   without ANALYZE to prevent double-execution side effects". This is incorrect for
   PostgreSQL — the adapter currently has NO DML guard (postgresql.py:704 always
   issues EXPLAIN ANALYZE regardless of query type). The DML-without-ANALYZE note
   accurately describes DuckDB (which has the guard), not PostgreSQL. PR #776
   incorrectly projected DuckDB behavior onto PostgreSQL.
   This is tracked as a separate correctness fix in query-plan-capture-postgresql-dml-guard.
   The docs note should be corrected to reflect reality: DuckDB has the guard;
   PostgreSQL does not yet; the fix is tracked separately.

Both corrections are documentation-only and do not change any code.

preserves.behavior: DuckDB platform section DML note must remain accurate — DuckDB already has the guard.

work_units.notes:
In the Performance Impact section, revise the "Other platforms" row to
distinguish ANALYZE and non-ANALYZE paths:
  | Platform | Overhead per query capture |
  |----------|---------------------------|
  | DuckDB (analyze_plans=True, default) | ~1× query execution time |
  | DuckDB (analyze_plans=False) | ~5-20ms (static EXPLAIN only) |
  | PostgreSQL (SELECT queries) | ~1× query execution time (EXPLAIN ANALYZE) |
  | PostgreSQL (DML queries) | ~10-50ms (EXPLAIN without ANALYZE, once guard lands) |
  | Redshift | ~10-50ms (plain EXPLAIN, no ANALYZE) |
  | MotherDuck | ~1× query execution time (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, same as DuckDB) |
Mark the PostgreSQL DML row with "(after query-plan-capture-postgresql-dml-guard)"
or a note that the guard is pending. Revise the prose that generalizes
~10-50ms to "ANALYZE-based adapters" vs "static EXPLAIN adapters".
work_units.summary: Correct the performance overhead table for PostgreSQL

work_units.notes:
The DML note currently says: "DML statements use FORMAT JSON without ANALYZE
to prevent double-execution side effects." Replace with:
  DuckDB guards DML queries by using FORMAT JSON without ANALYZE, avoiding
  double-execution. PostgreSQL's DML guard is pending
  (query-plan-capture-postgresql-dml-guard) — until then, DML queries
  with --capture-plans active will execute twice on PostgreSQL.
After query-plan-capture-postgresql-dml-guard is merged, revisit this note
to confirm it accurately describes both platforms.
